subject: Re: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - integration follow-up
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - integration follow-up

Hi Samir / Maya -

Thanks again for the call this morning - great to learn more about FinPay's routing and security constraints. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary / Goals
- Goal: Integrate Redwood inference into FinPay's private environment with predictable latency and no egress of sensitive PII outside approved networks.
- Focus areas from today's call: VPC endpoints (PrivateLink), IP allowlisting, egress/DNS, and mutual TLS (mTLS) for service-to-service traffic. Also covered SDK auth (API key vs OIDC), embeddings/reranker considerations, and structured output/tool-calling safety.

Integration checklist (high level)
1) Networking:
   - Configure an AWS VPC Endpoint (Interface) for Redwood Private control/data plane as discussed - we support PrivateLink and peered connectivity.
   - IP allowlist: Redwood will provide the egress IP ranges for the endpoint. FinPay needs to allow these ranges on inbound firewall rules for the endpoint (we'll provide exact CIDRs).
   - Ports: HTTPS (443) is sufficient for control and inference traffic; we recommend allowing outbound 443 to Redwood endpoint CIDRs.
   - DNS / Egress: If you use a private resolver, allow resolution of redwood-hosted domains or provide conditional forwarding to our DNS.
   - mTLS: We recommend mTLS for service authentication - Redwood can exchange certs with your SREs.

2) Auth & SDKs:
   - Short-term: API keys for initial testing (scoped, short TTL).
   - Long-term: OIDC/SAML-backed tokens for rotated credentials and improved auditability.
   - SDKs: We'll share a sample SDK init for embeddings + reranker with support for private endpoints.

3) Data handling & embeddings:
   - For embeddings/rerank flows where data must not leave your VPC, we support private deployment options that perform vectorization and reranking inside your network. We'll confirm the deployment model in the MAP.

Attachments: FP-VPC-Network-Diagram.pdf, mutual_action_plan_FP-0481.xlsx (attached)

Next steps / owners
- Jonas (cc'd) will send a short tech runbook with example mTLS steps, allowed CIDRs, and a sample nginx/proxy config by EOD 11/29.
- FinPay (Samir/Maya) to confirm internal network contact and whether there are VPN/proxy egress restrictions by 11/30.
- I'll schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week for network + security (please share availability).

If that looks right, I'll lock the MAP milestones and invite the right people to the technical call.

Thanks -
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwoodinference.com

- When you say "IP allowlist for the endpoint", do we need to allow the Redwood CIDRs inbound to our VPC endpoint, or is it outbound from our network to Redwood's managed endpoint? We're trying to map this to our current firewall rules.
- Ports: 443 is fine for the TLS tunnel, but do you foresee any additional port requirements for metrics/health checks?
- For embeddings/reranker: our compliance team prefers that raw text and vectors stay within our VPC. Can you confirm whether the hosted private option will keep embeddings generation + reranking inside our network?
- mTLS: can you share the cert exchange process and whether Redwood supports automated rotation (ACME-style) or if this is a manual upload?

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.com>, Maya Lopez <maya.lopez@finpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - integration follow-up

Hi Samir / Maya -

Quick technical notes and the runbook items Lauren mentioned. I'll keep this concise and paste examples you can hand to your network team.

1) IP directions & ports - Allow outbound HTTPS (443) from FinPay to the Redwood interface endpoint DNS name (we provide) or to the CIDRs below. For the interface endpoint model, traffic originates from your VPC and goes to the interface endpoint network interface in your VPC; you still control SGs and NACLs. If using PrivateLink to reach our managed NLB, we will provide the exact ENI CIDRs.

Example placeholder CIDRs we will use (final values will be in the MAP / runbook):
- 34.82.12.0/24
- 35.123.45.0/24

Ports: 443 for API + health checks. If you use Prometheus scraping, we can expose metrics on a separate port but recommend pulling via a metrics proxy rather than opening wide access.

2) DNS - If you have a private resolver, add a conditional forward for redwood-private.redwoodinference.com -> our resolver. Alternatively, we can provide the interface endpoint's private DNS name to resolve inside your VPC.

3) mTLS cert exchange (recommended flow)
- Option A (manual): FinPay generates CSR -> Redwood returns signed cert -> both sides upload certs to their respective endpoints; rotation performed on schedule (we recommend 90d).
- Option B (automated): We support automated rotation via an enterprise PKI integration (SAML/OIDC with cert provisioning) - requires additional setup; we can discuss on the call.

Sample curl to test mTLS (client cert + key):
curl --cert finpay-client.crt --key finpay-client.key \
  -H "Host: redwood-private.redwoodinference.com" \
  https://redwood-private.redwoodinference.com/healthz

4) SDK / Auth example (embeddings + reranker to private endpoint)
- Short-term (API key): set header Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> and point SDK base_url to the private endpoint.
- Long-term (OIDC): exchange code -> get access_token scoped to inference:embed and inference:rank. We'll send an example OIDC config for Keycloak/Azure AD.

5) Embeddings data locality
- For the Redwood Private deployment, vectorization and reranking can run inside your VPC/managed cluster so vectors never leave your network. We'll mark this as critical in the MAP.

Attached: FP-VPC-Network-Diagram.pdf (annotated)

I'll follow up with a short runbook (IP list, sample SG/NACL rules, and an nginx sidecar snippet) as a Drive link by EOD. If you want the immediate nginx reverse-proxy example, here is a minimal snippet:

# nginx example (proxy outbound to Redwood private endpoint)
# server block inside your app VPC
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  server_name internal-app.finpay.internal;

  ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/finpay.crt;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/finpay.key;

  location /api/ {
    proxy_pass https://redwood-private.redwoodinference.com/;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header Authorization "Bearer ${API_KEY}";
    proxy_ssl_trusted_certificate /etc/ssl/redwood-ca.pem;
    proxy_ssl_verify on;
  }
}

Happy to hop on a call to walk through this - suggest Tue 12/1 or Wed 12/2 afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Jonas
